interpretation_limits: Literal answers and native row answers share logical questions, not prompts, adapters or world-addressing workload.
Strict action-table correctness is global argmax equality, not a claim about all information in the soft row.
For a rendered action outside the offered menu, A/B correctness cannot demonstrate fidelity to the text.
D and ED are parallel reads of the emitted text; ED does not re-encode the literal reader's A/B answer.
ED preserves choices and hard action IDs here, not floating states or A/B scores.
Formal substitutions reuse only exact archived physical rows and do not establish unseen-form transfer.

hash_schemes.literal_question_sha256: SHA256(canonical JSON string), matching archived records.digest
hash_schemes.native_prompt_sha256: archived SHA256(canonical JSON token-ID list), not a text hash
hash_schemes.source_sha256: SHA256(canonical JSON string), matching archived records.digest
hash_schemes.utf8_sha256: SHA256(raw UTF-8 text bytes); explicitly suffixed companion fields

matching.uncertainty: descriptive_archival_counts; repeated world/order/style rows are not independent samples

examples.literal_question:
At decision time the left signal reads off. The right signal reads on. For these readings, which listed action follows the policy?
A = the earliest reports. B = the most recent reports. Respond with only A or B.
examples.rendered_text:
When the left signal is off and the right signal is off, I choose the most recent reports.
When the left signal is off and the right signal is on, I choose the earliest reports.
When the left signal is on and the right signal is off, I choose the earliest reports.
When the left signal is on and the right signal is on, I choose the earliest reports.
examples.source:
My regular choice here is the earliest reports.
My alternate choice here is the most recent reports.
The alternate choice is triggered when the left signal is off.
The regular choice overrides it when the right signal is on.
